resolvedQuestions.text: Where are a packet's problem, purpose and user need written today, per level and for a phase parent, and which of those places is required and validated?

For each hop surface, what does it read and what does it emit, and does the purpose travel? Surfaces: the Claude compaction hooks (`runtime/hooks/claude/compact-inject.ts`, `session-prime.ts`) and their counterparts for other runtimes under `runtime/hooks/`, `/speckit:resume`, `/speckit:handoff` and the session relaunch, `/speckit:save` with `generate-context.js`, the deep-loop iteration prompts and child-dispatch briefs.
In real packets under `specs/` that have a `handover.md` or several continuity saves, is the purpose restated, shortened or absent? Do phase children restate the parent's purpose or drift from it?

Which candidate change closes the measured gap at the lowest cost? The operator's candidates, to be tested and not assumed: acceptance criteria at the parent spec level, a user story or purpose and problem section at the parent level and an improved parent-specific spec template. Add any other candidate the evidence supports, for example a purpose field in the continuity block or in the compaction brief.
What is ruled out, and why?

keyFindings.text: Every authored spec level writes the problem and purpose exactly once, in one section: `## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE` with `### Problem Statement` and `### Purpose`. The core template carries it for Levels 1-3 and 3+ [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/core/spec.md.tmpl:99-107]; the phase-parent template carries the same two subsections [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/packet-types/phase-parent.spec.md.tmpl:63-72]; the research-record template carries it too [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/packet-types/research.spec.md.tmpl:57-67].

For a standard packet the only authored purpose carrier is `spec.md` §2 "PROBLEM & PURPOSE", which holds a Problem Statement and a one-sentence Purpose. The core template ships the `problem` anchor, and Level 2 requires the anchors `metadata, problem, scope, requirements, success-criteria, risks, questions`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/core/spec.md.tmpl:100-112] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/tests/template-structure.vitest.ts:74-83]

The `problem` anchor is enforced only as a structural presence check. A document stamped `SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE` v2.3 or later fails with `required anchor '<id>' is missing` for each anchor its rendered template requires; a v2.2 or unstamped document keeps integrity-only checking. Content inside the anchor is never graded beyond unfilled template tokens. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/validation/validation-rules.md:449] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/validation/validation-rules.md:57]

"User need" has no dedicated authored field at Levels 1-2. The only `As a … I want … so that …` surface is `## 11. USER STORIES`, emitted inside an `<!-- IF level:3,3+ -->` block [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/core/spec.md.tmpl:326-347]. At Levels 1-2 the user need exists only as prose inside the Problem Statement, so nothing structural distinguishes it from the problem description.

File-level requirements rise with level while the purpose carrier stays the same single section: Level 1 requires `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `implementation-summary.md`; Level 2 adds `acceptance-criteria.md`; Level 3 keeps that set with `decision-record.md` as a lazy add-on. No level requires a separate problem, purpose or user-story document. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/validation/validation-rules.md:218-223]

The level contract requires only mechanical docs. Levels 1-3 require `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`; `implementation-summary.md` becomes required only after implementation starts; `handover.md`, `goal.md`, `timeline.md`, `decision-record.md` and `research/research.md` are `lazyAddonDocs` (scaffolded only on request), and `acceptance-criteria.md` is an optional addon at Levels 2-3, required only through the separate `AC_CLOSURE` rule [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/spec-kit-docs.json:levels.1.requiredCoreDocs/lazyAddonDocs/optionalAddonDocs; .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/structure/folder-structure.md:158-190].

A phase parent is a weaker contract: `FILE_EXISTS` accepts only the lean trio `spec.md`, `description.json`, `graph-metadata.json`, and heavy docs live in the children. The parent therefore has exactly one prose document in which purpose could live. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/structure/phase-definitions.md:144-146] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/validation/validation-rules.md:226-228]

The phase level requires `spec.md` alone, and its section-gate table declares `problem` as required for `spec.md` at `phase` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/spec-kit-docs.json:levels.phase.requiredCoreDocs; levels.phase.sectionGates["spec.md"].problem]. So the declared contract does name the purpose section as required at parent level.

Required-section enforcement exists but is gated on the template stamp. `ANCHORS_VALID` requires every anchor whose template section is a required H2, but only for documents carrying a `SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE … v2.3` or newer stamp [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/validation/orchestrator.ts:758-768, 1028-1035]. A v2.4 `spec.md` that deletes the whole `PROBLEM & PURPOSE` section fails with a named missing anchor; an older, unstamped document keeps only the integrity check.

The phase-parent spec template does demand purpose at authoring time: its authoring contract lists "Root purpose: what problem does this entire phased decomposition solve?" as REQUIRED parent content, and its body has Problem Statement and Purpose subsections plus a note that this spec is the only authored parent document. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/packet-types/phase-parent.spec.md.tmpl:35-37] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/packet-types/phase-parent.spec.md.tmpl:65-71]

That parent purpose requirement is not validated. Phase parents are explicitly exempt from anchor checks, and the phase-parent template is stamped v2.2, so the v2.3+ required-anchor rule never fires for a parent. A parent can therefore ship with an empty or stale Problem & Purpose and still pass `--strict`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/validation/validation-rules.md:443] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/packet-types/phase-parent.spec.md.tmpl:80]

The phase parent is explicitly exempt from that check, so the parent's declared `problem` requirement is not executed. `ANCHORS_VALID` returns early for a folder classified as a phase parent with `'Phase parent lean document set accepted'` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/validation/orchestrator.ts:963-970]. The other sufficiency loop enforces missing anchors only for `timeline.md` and `goal.md` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/validation/spec-doc-structure.ts:1182-1191]. Net effect: a phase parent's `spec.md` can lose Problem & Purpose entirely and still validate.

No validation rule reads the purpose prose. Grep counts for `problem` are zero across the validator modules (measured this iteration), and the only content-shaped checks are placeholder tokens (`PLACEHOLDER_FILLED`) and the non-empty-anchor-body check, which fires only when an anchor is present and empty [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/validation/orchestrator.ts:752-756, 889-899; .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/validation/spec-doc-structure.ts:1193-1200]. A spec that keeps the section and writes a vacuous sentence passes.

Two secondary purpose carriers exist but neither is required. `goal.md`'s "Durable Directive" asks for one sentence on "What this packet is for", yet `goal.md` is absent from every level's required-file list and is authored only on request through the goal workflow. `description.json` carries a one-line `description`, which is the only purpose-shaped field present at every level including a phase parent. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/addons/goal.md.tmpl:38-41] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/validation/validation-rules.md:218-228] [SOURCE: specs/system-speckit/spec-authoring-and-continuity/006-purpose-retention-across-handovers/description.json:2-9]

`goal.md` is the only surface with a durable one-line statement of intent: `## 1. DURABLE DIRECTIVE` / `**Objective:** [One sentence. What this packet is for…]`, and its anchors are required whenever the document exists [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/addons/goal.md.tmpl:38-41; .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/validation/spec-doc-structure.ts:242-246]. It is a lazy addon, so a packet that did not ask for it has no durable directive at all [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/spec-kit-docs.json:levels.1.lazyAddonDocs].

No template or validator surface uses the term "user need". A repository-wide search over templates, commands, runtime and the research packet found the phrase only in this packet's own spec and tasks; the nearest authored slot is the one-sentence Purpose, and the nearest machine-readable slot is the one-line `description.json` description. [INFERENCE: based on a case-insensitive search of .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit, .skilled/commands/speckit, .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop and specs/system-speckit for "user need", "whom it serves" and "who it serves", which returned hits only in packet 006 and its baseline copies] [SOURCE: specs/system-speckit/spec-authoring-and-continuity/006-purpose-retention-across-handovers/spec.md:36]

The continuity record that every save writes has no purpose field at all. `ThinContinuityRecord` is exactly `packet_pointer`, `last_updated_at`, `last_updated_by`, `recent_action`, `next_safe_action`, `blockers`, `key_files`, `session_dedup`, `session_ref`, `completion_pct`, `open_questions`, `answered_questions`; the closest purpose-like slot is `next_safe_action`, which is an action, not a reason. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/continuity/thin-continuity-record.ts:60-73]

The two successor-facing surfaces carry no purpose field. `handover.md` has sections Handover Summary, Context Transfer, For Next Session, Validation Checklist, Session Notes and no problem/purpose heading [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/addons/handover.md.tmpl:37,50,84,107,121]; the `_memory.continuity` block carries `recent_action`, `next_safe_action`, `blockers`, `key_files`, `completion_pct`, `open_questions`, `answered_questions` and no purpose or problem key [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/core/implementation-summary.md.tmpl:38-63]. `acceptance-criteria.md` likewise has no purpose column: `AC-ID`, `REQ`, `Given / When / Then`, `Verification`, `Status`, `Waiver` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/addons/acceptance-criteria.md.tmpl:57-66].

Claude's PreCompact hook reads only the live transcript tail. It extracts active file paths, recent topics, working-memory attention signals and the last five meaningful transcript lines, adds a detected `Active spec folder: <path>` line, and merges those into a token-budgeted brief [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/compact-inject.ts:443-492]. It opens no packet document: spec.md, handover.md and the continuity block are never read on this path, so the packet arrives as a path string and nothing else.

The startup hop carries no purpose. When no cached brief exists, `session-prime` returns a fixed surface whose only state line is "Continuity: recover on demand from the packet docs", plus two recovery tools (`/speckit:resume`, a ripgrep over `specs/`). No packet field is read and no purpose is emitted. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/session-prime.ts:230-251]

Net travel of purpose across the seven hop surfaces: startup carries none; compaction carries none except an action mislabeled "Goal"; resume has no purpose slot and inconsistently reads spec.md; handoff has a Goal slot but depends on the writer restating it; save carries none and descends past a phase parent; the deep-loop prompt carries a free-text topic; the child brief carries none. Only the handoff Goal and the compaction "Goal" facet use a purpose vocabulary, and neither reads `spec.md`'s Problem & Purpose. [INFERENCE: derived from findings 1-9 above]

`/speckit:save`'s writer contract is explicitly compact and mechanics-only: the documented payload fields are `recent_action` and `next_safe_action` (≤96 chars / ≤16 words), `blockers` and `key_files` (≤5 short items), plus the stored `completion_pct` and question lists [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/continuity/generate-context.ts:170-181]. The thin record has no purpose field [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/continuity/thin-continuity-record.ts:60-78], so a purpose survives a save only as a packet document, never as continuity state.

The deep-loop hop is the exception: the child-dispatch brief carries purpose-shaped text. `buildLoopPrompt` injects `research_topic: <full topic>` into the child prompt [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:1655-1669], and the per-iteration prompt pack renders `Research Topic: {research_topic}` plus focus and remaining questions on every iteration [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/assets/prompt-pack-iteration.md.tmpl:11-16]. A research loop therefore restates its purpose by construction; an ordinary implementation session has no equivalent field at any hop.

The Claude pre-compaction hook's transcript analysis emits exactly three sections: `## Active Files`, `## Recent Topics` and `## Recent Context` (the last five meaningful transcript lines). Nothing reconstructs the project's why from the packet. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/compact-inject.ts:365-384]

The hook has a continuity-aware path, but it is opt-in: `authoredSnapshotEnabled(input)` is true only when the hook input sets `authored_continuity_snapshot: true` or `continuity_snapshot: 'authored'` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/compact-inject.ts:348-355]. Default compaction does not pass that flag, so the authored snapshot worker is skipped [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/compact-inject.ts:608-630].

Even on the continuity path the injected facets carry no purpose. `buildContinuityFacets` fills the facet labelled "Goal" from `next_safe_action`, "Decision" from answered-question ids, "Progress" from `recent_action` + summary + touched files, and "Gotcha" from blockers + open questions [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/continuity/thin-continuity-record.ts:289-303]. The renderer then prints those four headings with the literal labels `Goal`, `Decision`, `Progress`, `Gotcha` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/continuity/thin-continuity-record.ts:307-323]. So the one line a compacted session reads under the word "Goal" is the next action, which is the exact substitution the operator reported.

Every runtime adapter follows the same post-compaction shape: a summary plus `Active Spec Folder`, an optional history lookup and a `Recovery` pointer instructing `/speckit:resume`. The dsh adapter composes base context + lookup + recovery pointer; the pi adapter composes `Post-Compaction Summary`, `Active Spec Folder`, lookup and recovery pointer; devin has the same recovery-pointer builder. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/dsh/session-compact-context.mjs:126-142] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/pi/session-compact-context.ts:148-165] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/devin/post-compaction.cjs:265-285]

`session-prime.ts` emits pointers, not content. At startup its fallback surface is the continuity line `- Continuity: recover on demand from the packet docs` plus `/speckit:resume — recover the active packet from its canonical docs` and the `rg` hint [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/session-prime.ts:230-258]; after a compaction it prints `Context was compacted. Run /speckit:resume against the active packet to recover session state.` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/session-prime.ts:135-170]. Recovery is delegated to the packet docs; the hook itself never states what the packet is for.

The authored-continuity snapshot injected at compaction has a facet labeled "Goal", but the builder fills that facet from `next_safe_action`. The rendered block is therefore `### Goal` followed by an imperative action, not by the packet's purpose; the other facets are answers, progress and blockers. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/continuity/thin-continuity-record.ts:289-303] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/continuity/thin-continuity-record.ts:307-313] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/continuity/authored-continuity-snapshot.ts:104-115]

`/speckit:resume` emits a resume packet with the slots `now|last|next|blockers|artifact`, and its recovery ladder is handover.md (<24h) → `_memory.continuity` → supporting spec docs → ripgrep recipes. The ladder names spec.md among supporting docs, but the `context_loading_priority` order and the step-2 activity list substitute `tasks/plan/decision-record/resource-map` and omit spec.md. The intent-carrying document is therefore read only on the branch the workflow contradicts itself about, and even when read it maps to no purpose slot. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/assets/speckit-resume-auto.yaml:92-93] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/assets/speckit-resume-auto.yaml:106-110] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/assets/speckit-resume-auto.yaml:159-174]

The other runtimes split into two groups, and neither group recovers purpose. Codex's PreCompact adapter hands the event to the Claude implementation (`runClaudeHookAdapter('compact-inject.js', …)`) [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/codex/compact-inject.ts:36-38]. DSH's compaction handler reuses the shared session-prime output as its base context and appends the same `/speckit:resume` recovery pointer [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/dsh/session-compact-context.mjs:7,122,126-142], where that prime output is the spawned Claude session-prime hook's stdout [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/dsh/session-start-context.mjs:44-58]. Pi and Devin compose their own recovery sections: the retained compaction summary, `## Active Spec Folder\n<path>`, and `## Recovery\nRun /speckit:resume …` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/pi/session-compact-context.ts:141-190; .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/devin/post-compaction.cjs:266-290]. No hook outside Claude imports the authored-snapshot module, and no hook calls the resume ladder at all (grep over `runtime/hooks` found one importer, `claude/compact-inject.ts:40`).

`/speckit:handoff` and the session relaunch are the one hop with a purpose-shaped slot. The note format is fixed as `## Goal`, `## Done`, `## Remaining work`, `## In-flight state`, and the instruction defines Goal as "states what the work is for". The note is hand-authored; `prepare` only adds an optional `goal_packet` pointer when it can prove the packet's `goal.md` holds the active goal. Purpose therefore travels only when the writer restates it or a `goal.md` exists to be pointed at. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/handoff.md:104-131] [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-relaunch/bin/session-relaunch.cjs:822]

`/speckit:resume` parses each tier into a fixed signal shape that has no purpose field: `summary`, `recentAction`, `nextSafeAction`, `blockers`, `keyFiles`, `documents`, plus an optional `packetPointer` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/resume/resume-ladder.ts:56-72]. The handover tier reads only the labelled values `Recent action`, `Next safe action`, `Blockers`, `Key files` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/resume/resume-ladder.ts:632-673]; the continuity tier maps the thin record's six fields into the same shape [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/resume/resume-ladder.ts:677-712].

`/speckit:save` through `generate-context.js` writes action and state, never purpose. Its `--full-auto` continuity fields are `recent_action`, `next_safe_action`, `blockers`, `key_files`, `completion_pct`, `open_questions` and `answered_questions`, and the writer upserts them into the leaf's `implementation-summary.md` or a research record's `spec.md`. A save aimed at a phase parent descends one level per save to the leaf, so the parent's Problem & Purpose is neither refreshed nor checked by the save path. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js:133-146] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js:76-80] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js:610-680]

The spec-docs fallback tier cannot recover purpose either. It takes the title plus the first three non-heading, non-table lines as the summary, and *synthesizes* the next action as `Review tasks.md and continue the packet.` or `Review <primary>.md and continue the packet.` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/resume/resume-ladder.ts:758-790; collectSummaryLines at :405-417]. A packet's Problem & Purpose paragraph can reach the brief only by happening to sit inside those first three plain body lines — `## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE` is a heading and is filtered out.

The deep-loop iteration prompt carries `Research Topic`, `Focus Area`, `Remaining Key Questions`, carried-forward questions, last-three-iteration summaries, pivot lineage and saturated directions. There is no purpose field; the free-text research topic is the only channel that can carry a why, and a caller may pass a bare topic label. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/assets/prompt-pack-iteration.md.tmpl:10-20]

The operator-facing brief has no purpose row: `RESUME BRIEF` renders Spec, Confidence, Source, Now, Last confirmed, Next safe action, Blockers, Progress and "Why this is next" [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/assets/speckit-resume-presentation.txt:116-129]. The restore panel that feeds it is capped at 8 items and 1,200 characters and is built from the same four facets, so a purpose string would compete with next-action and key-file items for the same budget [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/resume/resume-ladder.ts:507-560].

Child-dispatch briefs have a documented content contract and it carries no purpose. The brief must name the files and symbols to read, what has already been tried, the frozen scope and the question, and must exclude the dispatcher's preferred conclusion. The packet's problem, purpose and user need are absent from both the required and the forbidden lists. [SOURCE: .skilled/repo-rules/delegation-and-orchestration.md:80] [SOURCE: .skilled/repo-rules/delegation-and-orchestration.md:96-100]

`/speckit:handoff` saves continuity before writing the note and hands the receiving session to `/speckit:resume` [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/handoff.md:42,61,78-88], and the handover template has no purpose heading [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/addons/handover.md.tmpl:37,50,84,107,121]. Even an author who adds a purpose paragraph has no reader: the handover parser looks only for four labelled fields, so the paragraph can travel only accidentally through `collectSummaryLines` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/resume/resume-ladder.ts:632-640,405-417].

Packet-level `handover.md` uses the handover addon shape (`## 1. Handover Summary`, `## 2. Context Transfer`, `## 3. For Next Session`), not the relaunch-note shape with a `## Goal` section. Its heading set has no slot for the problem or purpose: it records what shipped, decisions, blockers, files, traps, a starting point and remaining tasks. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/addons/handover.md.tmpl:37-84]

keyFindings.text: Purpose is authored at spec level and usually filled. Of 3,294 live `spec.md` files, 3,211 carry the `problem` anchor; 2,943 carry filled `### Purpose` text, 22 still carry a template placeholder, and 246 have the anchor with an empty Purpose subsection (measured by the extraction script described above). The section exists and is used; the purpose is not a missing authoring surface.

sources: Parent/child ### Purpose comparison over specs/**/spec.md (297 parents, 1,029 pairs, 2026-11-13)

keyFindings.text: Parent-level purpose is already authored in two machine-readable carriers, and neither is the artifact the operator proposed. The phase-parent template carries `## 2. The phase-parent template ships §2 PROBLEM & PURPOSE with Problem Statement and Purpose and marks root purpose as REQUIRED parent content. What is missing is a real value and a reader: 68 parents have an empty Purpose, 8 hold the scaffold placeholder, and 4 hold create.sh's generic text, so 80 of 297 parents carry no real why. keyFindings.text: Candidate (c), an improved parent-specific template, cannot close the gap on its own for the same reason: the parent template already carries the purpose and the missing piece is a reader. A user-story block could ride along in the same edit as a read-side change, but as a standalone candidate it changes authoring only.

Candidate D, a purpose field in the `_memory.continuity` block, reaches more hops per unit of change than any other candidate. The block is already present in 2,857 of 2,870 implementation summaries, is the second rung of the resume ladder, and is rendered into the compaction snapshot by `buildContinuityFacets`. keyFindings.text: Candidate (d), a purpose field in the continuity block, is the most expensive. It needs the thin-record interface and its `MEMORY_0NN` validation, the compact serializer, the save writer's documented payload contract, the implementation-summary template and the resume parser, plus a fallback story for the 4,657 existing `implementation-summary.md` files that have no such field [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/continuity/thin-continuity-record.ts:60-78; .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/continuity/generate-context.ts:170-181]. It also leaves the 29 handover-only packets uncovered.

Candidate D's cost is bounded to one subsystem and has no corpus migration. The touch points are the `ThinContinuityRecord` interface and validator, the `generate-context.js` payload/help fields and carry path, the `buildContinuityFacets` source, and their tests. The field can be optional with a fallback, so no existing packet fails validation and no new required file appears. The value can be sourced from the packet's own `spec.md` Purpose, or from the nearest ancestor with a real purpose when the packet is a phase child, using the same parent walk the save path already performs for phase-parent pointers. keyFindings.text: Candidate (e), a purpose line in the compaction brief, is feasible and cheap on Claude: the active packet is resolvable without the transcript because `lastSpecFolder` is persisted in hook state [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/hook-state.ts:345], so one extra file read supplies the purpose. It covers only the compaction hop, and pi/devin compose their own sections, so it needs per-runtime wiring [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/devin/post-compaction.cjs:270-290].

Candidate E, a purpose line in the resume or compaction payload, is cheaper per file but weaker in coverage: the compaction brief is built from transcript analysis and would need a disk read inside a hook with a tight budget, while the resume output contract is a presentation change that only helps the resume hop. It is a complement to D, not a substitute: once the continuity block carries purpose, both surfaces can read it with no extra packet read. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/compact-inject.ts:365-384] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/assets/speckit-resume-auto.yaml:169-174]

keyFindings.text: Candidate (f), one purpose row on the resume surface, is the smallest change that closes the measured gap. The ladder already reads `spec.md` among its spec-doc snapshots before it chooses a primary tier [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/resume/resume-ladder.ts:1128-1141], and its signal shape is one interface plus one renderer [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/lib/resume/resume-ladder.ts:56-72; .skilled/commands/speckit/assets/speckit-resume-presentation.txt:116-129]. Cost: two files and one test — add `purpose` to the signal, extract `### Purpose` from the snapshot already in memory (falling back to an author-labelled `**Objective:**` line when present, of which the corpus has one example [SOURCE: specs/system-deep-loop/z_archive/022-sk-deep-research-evolution/005-sk-deep-research-review-mode/handover.md:33]), and render a `Purpose:` row in the RESUME BRIEF. No schema change, no migration, no new authoring.

The smallest authoring-side fix that pairs with D is a two-line generator change: stop substituting a generic parent purpose in `create.sh` and let the template placeholder reach the file, so `PLACEHOLDER_FILLED` fails a Draft parent until a real why is authored; bump the phase-parent stamp to v2.4 in the same change so the parent gains the required `problem` anchor, grandfathering existing parents under the documented tolerant policy. This closes the 80-of-297 authoring gap without a new document and without retrofitting the backlog. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh:1875-1876] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/packet-types/phase-parent.spec.md.tmpl:80] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/validation/validation-rules.md:228]

keyFindings.text: Candidate (f) is also the widest coverage per unit of effort, because every runtime's recovery surface already delegates to `/speckit:resume`: Claude's compaction output tells the session to run it [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/claude/session-prime.ts:135-170], dsh appends the same pointer [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/dsh/session-compact-context.mjs:122,126-142], and devin and pi emit `## Recovery\nRun /speckit:resume …` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/devin/post-compaction.cjs:266]. One read-side addition therefore reaches every hop the operator described, and it also fixes the misleading facet label from iteration 2 by making the real purpose available next to the next action.

Ranked by coverage per unit of migration risk: D first, the generator/stamp fix second, E third, B as the content prerequisite it always was, and A last. The evidence does not support any candidate that adds a new parent-level document; it supports making the existing parent purpose real and making the existing continuity block carry it. [INFERENCE: ranking from findings 1-8 and the measured failure points]

keyFindings.text: The interactive `/speckit:resume` brief is not produced by the programmatic ladder. The command workflow carries its own continuity ladder — read `handover.md`, then `_memory.continuity`, then the canonical spec docs, then a ripgrep recipe only for a named gap [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/assets/speckit-resume-auto.yaml:105-112] — and its reply format fixes the visible fields at `Confidence`, `Context source`, `Now`, `Last confirmed`, `Next safe action` [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/speckit/assets/speckit-resume-auto.yaml:138]. `Purpose` is not among them.

Ruled out — using validation as the lever: the only executed required-anchor check exempts phase parents, and the phase level's declared `problem` gate is never executed, so a validation change would enforce authoring at the parent while leaving every hop untouched. It is a different change from the one the evidence supports, and it would not close the measured gap.

The user-need half of the problem is absent even where purpose is written. Of 2,866 real Purpose paragraphs, 333 (11.6%) mention a user, operator, reader or other beneficiary; Problem Statements do better at 623 of 2,884 (21.6%) but still leave four in five silent about whom the work serves. Any carried value must therefore include the Problem Statement, not only the Purpose sentence, or the who is still lost. [INFERENCE: based on beneficiary-word scans over specs/**/spec.md, run 2026-11-13]

keyFindings.text: Stress test of the recommendation: a continuity `purpose` field survives the failure modes if (a) the writer always attempts population with a leaf → nearest-ancestor fallback, using the parent walk the save already performs; (b) an unset value renders as an explicit "not recorded" marker rather than a generic sentence; (c) the field is optional, so no existing record fails validation; and (d) the authoring fix lands, because a phase child whose parent purpose is empty has nothing to inherit.
